result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.average_neighbor_degree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute average neighbor degree for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L15450-L15605){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.average_neighbor_degree( source="out", target="out", weight=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For each node, calculates the average degree of its neighbors. This metric helps analyze degree correlations and mixing patterns in networks, indicating whether nodes tend to connect to similar-degree neighbors (assortative) or different-degree neighbors (disassortative). For undirected graphs, computes the average degree of all neighbors. For directed graphs, the `source` parameter controls which neighbors to consider, and the `target` parameter controls how to measure their degrees. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : For directed graphs only, specifies which neighbors to consider: (1) `"out"` for out-neighbors (successors), (2) `"in"` for in-neighbors (predecessors), and (3) `"in+out"` for both in-neighbors and out-neighbors. Raises error if used with undirected graphs. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["out"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : For directed graphs only, specifies how to measure neighbor degrees: (1) `"out"` for out-neighbors (successors), (2) `"in"` for in-neighbors (predecessors), and (3) `"in+out"` for both in-neighbors and out-neighbors. Raises error if used with undirected graphs. [weight]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge attribute name containing weights. If provided, computes weighted average using: `k_nn,i = (1 / s_i) * Σ_j w_ij * k_j`, where `s_i` is the weighted degree. Currently not implemented and will raise error if specified. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of node attribute to store results. If `None`, uses `average_neighbor_degree`. Only used when `return_dict=False`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dict mapping node labels to average neighbor degrees. If `False`, stores values in graph and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=True`: dictionary mapping node ID to average neighbor degree. If `return_dict=False`: self (for method chaining). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : - if graph is empty - if `source` or `target` parameters are used with undirected graphs - if `source` or `target` values are invalid - if `weight` is specified (not yet implemented) ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - measures degree correlation patterns in networks - high values indicate nodes connect to high-degree neighbors (assortative mixing) - low values indicate nodes connect to low-degree neighbors (disassortative mixing) - for undirected graphs, ignores `source` and `target` parameters - nodes with no neighbors have average neighbor degree of `0` - weighted version not yet implemented ## Examples {.doc-examples} **Path Graph - Undirected** ::: {#18bf02a5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # In a path graph, end nodes have neighbors with degree 1, # middle nodes have neighbors with varying degrees g = ec.Graph(directed=False) for i in range(5): g.add_node(label=str(i)) for i in range(4): g.add_edge(str(i), str(i+1)) and_values = g.average_neighbor_degree(return_dict=True) # Node '0': neighbor '1' has degree 2 -> average = 2.0 # Node '1': neighbors '0','2' have degrees 1,2 -> average = 1.5 # Node '2': neighbors '1','3' have degrees 2,2 -> average = 2.0 ``` ::: **Directed Graph - Different source/target combinations** ::: {#3945a00c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=True) g.add_node(label='A') g.add_node(label='B') g.add_node(label='C') g.add_edge('A', 'B') g.add_edge('B', 'C') g.add_edge('C', 'A') # Average out-degree of out-neighbors and_out_out = g.average_neighbor_degree(source="out", target="out", return_dict=True) # Average in-degree of in-neighbors and_in_in = g.average_neighbor_degree(source="in", target="in", return_dict=True) ``` ::: **Store in Graph and Chain** ::: {#859414c8 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label='A') .add_node(label='B') .add_node(label='C') .add_edge('A', 'B') .add_edge('B', 'C') .average_neighbor_degree(attr_name='knn') ) # Values stored as node attribute 'knn' ``` :::
